chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Ted Jr. on the fad for hiring black music teachers
summary: Hinton asks about a Bird play and jazz curricula; Ted Jr. recalls being phased out of City University when the 1970s fad for black music ended.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, Steve Wilson -- do any of you three guys want to get on with your dad, because I know it will be interesting in years to come to know how progressive you are and how you all are looking at this, which to me is just wonderful.
But do you really think that perhaps we're looking

for it to continue like with the Basie thing, or are we looking for it to expand? Could you envision perhaps, with people coming out of these colleges, perhaps the drama department could get together with the music department of a school and write a play about Bird and produce it on Broadway, and then you might have a new trend of jazz coming from that angle? Can you envision that kind of thing?

Well, where I was teaching -- no. I find that there is just tremendous rivalry from one department to the next, each trying to claim credit for worthless nothing, having very little regard for quality, for the past history of jazz, in particular, you know, during the 1970's, particularly from 1970, there was this big wave of, quote, 'black music', of hiring black professors to teach black music, it was just all a fad, and it wore out.

I am one of many so-called black teachers or professors that just got phased right out. We were necessary for the politics of the time, and then after trends changed, the war disappeared, the Civil Rights movement sort of faded out, and they said, okay, now we don't need these guys any more, so just get rid of them.

Some who were smart enough and who knew better, had better experiences secured themselves at the beginning, and they're still going now, but for most, like in my particular situation, I didn't know that was coming, and so my particular environment in the City University in New York, I think not.

From what I've read, though, in educational journals, I think schools further out west, like maybe some of the big heavily sponsored schools like Eastman and so forth, they have outstanding programs, and it's posible that in those areas, what you suggested might take place may even be taking place.
